chartInvestigation.scope: Instrumented unchanged production build with real isolated Auth sessions
chartInvestigation.serverChart: Money in, money out and the net for 12 months
chartInvestigation.finding: Intermittent Next client search-parameter transition stalls after the correct server response; also reproduced a 65-second timeout, and observed an aborted RSC request in another attempt. Both successful and stalled transitions occurred with standard 3600-second tokens. Neither changing token duration nor waiting for document load fixes it.
chartInvestigation.correction: Only range links use native document navigation, anchored at the chart. A chart-control mount effect restores that anchor after streamed content arrives. Existing searchParams parsing, SVG rendering, RPC and calculations are unchanged. The twelve-month axis keeps six spaced labels, with all twelve data buckets and tooltips retained; the six-month view is unchanged.
chartInvestigation.limit: No claim about the precise internal Next.js scheduler cause; the failure is localized to client navigation rather than chart data or search parameter parsing.

passwordFormInvestigation.scope: Real browser submissions of the signed-in change-password form against the disposable stack; all writes synthetic
passwordFormInvestigation.baselineComponent: ChangePasswordForm: useActionState(changePassword); the form action also drove useFormStatus
passwordFormInvestigation.instrumentation: An unchanged build with one added client log of the value the action promise resolved with

baselineReproduction.finding: The action promise resolved with "Your current password is incorrect." on all 16 attempts, so the result reached the browser every time. The form displayed it on 7. Display matched, one for one, the attempts where a client tree update followed the 200 response.

passwordFormInvestigation.cause: useActionState does not render the value its own action function already returned to the client: it publishes that value through an app-router tree update, and on these profile pages the update commits only intermittently. The promise is reliable; the commit is not.
passwordFormInvestigation.secondFinding: Moving the result into component state but keeping the form`s `action` prop fixed the message and left the control stuck: `useFormStatus` clears its pending state through the same update, so the button stayed disabled on "Saving…" after an error that had already rendered. The submission is therefore handled in `onSubmit`, with both the result and the busy state held locally.
passwordFormInvestigation.correction: The form awaits the action, holds the result in component state and owns its busy state. A synchronous in-flight ref refuses a second submit. Field errors, the success banner, dropped requests and server failures are all rendered from that result. The action, its server-side re-authentication, the one-use verified-completion proof, the audit and the session handling are unchanged; no password check moved to the browser.
passwordFormInvestigation.cost: This form now needs JavaScript. The form action previously let it submit without it.
passwordFormInvestigation.limit: No claim is made about the internal Next.js cause. The defect is localized to the client application of server-action results, and is the same one behind BKC-02 and BKC-03.

collectionInvestigation.scope: Savings collection through the field officer screen, in a real browser against the disposable stack; all postings synthetic
collectionInvestigation.baselineComponent: RecordCollectionDialog: useActionState(recordMemberCollection); the confirmation screen rendered from state.ok

baselineMeasurement.component: RecordCollectionDialog - the field officer savings collection
baselineMeasurement.measured: 2 of 10 real postings on the stack that had already run a full certification; 15 of 15 confirmed on the final clean stack; the browser regression`s own Collections check failed once in two runs
baselineMeasurement.effect: The transaction was written to the ledger every time. In the failures the "Savings recorded" dialog never appeared, so the person at the counter saw no confirmation for money that had been taken.
baselineMeasurement.risk: The per-form idempotency key stops a resubmission of the same open dialog, but a fresh dialog carries a new key, so a re-entered collection would post twice.

collectionInvestigation.cause: The same client tree-update defect as BKC-02, BKC-03 and BKC-04. The action posts and its promise resolves with the result; useActionState publishes that result through an app-router update which, on this page, commits only intermittently. The ledger was correct in every observed failure; only the confirmation was lost.
collectionInvestigation.correction: useSubmission awaits the call and holds the outcome in component state; ActionForm wires it to the form; SubmitButton reads its pending state from that form rather than from useFormStatus. The action, the RPC, the posting rules, the reference, the approval requirements and the calculations are unchanged.
collectionInvestigation.outcomes: Three, never silence: carried out (with reference and receipt), refused (with the server message), or unresolved. Unresolved keeps the submission FormData and its idempotency key and offers only a re-send of that same submission; the posting functions return the original row for a key already seen, so the re-send either reports the posting that happened or performs the one that never did.
collectionInvestigation.regressionIntroducedAndFixed: Converting both branches to the same component let React reuse one DOM button, so the clicked "Review" became type="submit" mid-click and posted a collection from the editing step. Found by the new suite before release; fixed with distinct keys and a phase guard.

authoritativeRun.coverage: field officer, cashier and manager at 390px and 1440px, fifteen apiece, plus a slow answer, three clicks during one slow request, a lost answer for a posting that happened, a lost answer for one that never arrived, a refusal and a reload after a confirmed collection, each at both viewports

assertedEveryAttempt: exactly one ledger row carries the submission idempotency key

the member balance moved by the amount recorded and no more

terminatedRun.note: An earlier run on the previous build was stopped by the operator mid-run; the twenty recorded failures are all "browser has been closed" from that termination, not product failures. Retained as baseline/collection-terminated-run.json and not counted as a result.

collectionInvestigation.limit: No claim is made about the internal Next.js cause. The defect is localized to the client application of server-action results.

remainingExposure.title: The duplicate an idempotency key cannot stop
remainingExposure.scope: Investigated and documented; no database change made
remainingExposure.finding: The key protects one form instance. Closing the dialog, reopening it and entering the same payment generates a new key, and the database has no reason to refuse it.
remainingExposure.existingGuard: Merchant and bank collections must carry the external reference from the confirmation message, and record_member_collection refuses a reference already recorded against a live transaction. Cash collections require no reference, so nothing stops a second entry.
remainingExposure.proposal: Have the posting function refuse - or require an explicit override - when the same member, type, amount and value date are posted twice within a few minutes. It should refuse rather than silently de-duplicate, so a genuine second payment of the same amount can still be recorded deliberately. Not implemented here: it changes financial database behaviour and needs its own authorization and review.
remainingExposure.interimMitigation: The unresolved screen tells the person not to re-enter the payment and to check the member statement first.
remainingExposure.formsLeftNote: Configuration, member-record and account-administration forms. None posts to the ledger; each is recoverable by reloading the page. Listed with reasons in docs/financial-form-audit.md.
